decisions.evidence: It's a pleasure is the grammatical expression; As a pleasure lacks a predicate.
Sandy is an established repository nickname for prototype Sandeep, so both forms are plausible spoken address and must not be normalized to final-name Mirage.
Neither revision forms the likely direct address to Ivy: Tyree is wrong, while You lost Ivy is missing are and has broken punctuation.
Vindicta is authoritative and the later official line independently confirms the same name; its Hidden King ending remains separate.
The Hornet mapping and authoritative character vocabulary require Vindicta; Vendicta is misspelled.
Uh is an audible filler and cannot be added or removed from scene context alone.
I've brought biscuits for you and your guests, miss is the most coherent servant-delivery line, but brought/bought and guest number remain audible differences.
I won't hear the end of this at work is the established idiom and fits Haze's embarrassment; the alternatives are malformed.
Every one of our enemies is the complete grammatical noun phrase; Everyone our enemies is malformed.
That you win and the W are distinct, grammatical spoken endings; the third option is corrupt but does not resolve the first two.
A change of plans is needed is grammatical; I'm a change of plans is not.
Oh and Ah represent different audible interjections and cannot be inferred from the item-check filename.
Both component revisions are semantically and syntactically garbled; neither gives a defensible Calico concern line.
The filename and authoritative character list require Lash; Nash is a phonetic error.
Swap is the ability-related verb and standard spelling; swop conflicts with repository terminology and lowercase sentence guidance.
Ready and I'm ready differ by a spoken subject/contraction and both are natural ability-point reminders.
The Hornet mapping and authoritative character vocabulary require Vindicta.
We got and we've got are distinct spoken dialect/contraction forms; both are coherent Wraith concern lines.
The Baxter Society is an established lore organization tied to Shiv; backs of society is a phonetic corruption.
The world's and the elliptical World's differ by a spoken article, and both can function as a combat quip.
Good luck to you and your future endeavors and good luck to you in your future endeavors are both grammatical but audibly different.
Fur and electricity is the contextual joke when furry Mo and Krill are killed by electric Seven; fire loses that character-specific meaning.
The filename and vocabulary require direct address to Wraith; brave is a phonetic substitution.
Both generated revisions are garbled around the father's action; the later Archmother official line is entirely separate dialogue and cannot repair them.
This will and this'll are an exact spoken contraction distinction; both questions are grammatical.
Tryin' and trying encode pronunciation/register and cannot be selected from grammar.
Sucking and suckin' encode pronunciation/register; both match the vacuum ability.
Bebop missing is a valid elliptical ping and Bebop's missing a valid contraction; the garbled third revision does not distinguish them.
Neither The Fen orange nor The Fend Orange expresses the defend-Orange command indicated by the filename.
Both component revisions garble both Stun and authoritative Infernus; neither expresses the filename's command.
'Em and them are distinct audible forms and both fit Abrams's ability quip.
Because and cause are distinct spoken forms; both produce a coherent scene sentence.
Neither component revision uses authoritative Tempest; the correct Tempest revision lies outside the component.
The presence of Oh and the them/'em pronunciation are audible differences across otherwise plausible ability lines.
Neither Vendict nor Vendictus is authoritative Vindicta, so neither component revision is correct.
Pullin' and pulling encode audible pronunciation/register and cannot be selected from filename context.
The explicit filename and authoritative character spelling require Holliday.
Both revisions are ungrammatical and fail to name Cadence in the was-here ping.
The filename requires Stun Holliday; Stan and Stand are both incorrect commands despite correct character spelling.
The filename requires Stun Holliday; Stan and Stand are both incorrect commands.
What a bastard! is a coherent reaction to ally Lash's massive stomp; What's a bastard? changes it into an irrelevant definition question.
None of the component revisions names Wraith; the correct Wraith revision exists outside the component.
Revision 0 lowercases the proper character name Pocket, while revision 1 pluralizes it; neither existing component text is fully correct.
The filename and authoritative character vocabulary require Viscous; Viscus is misspelled.
Santin, Santy, and Santi do not preserve historical prototype Sandeep/Sandy from the filename.
Synth maps to the singular proper character Pocket; lowercase plural pockets is not the name.
Every component revision misspells Wrecker; the correct noncomponent revision cannot be selected for this component.
Man, beast, machine is a parallel singular enumeration and there's nothing I can't kill is grammatical; revision 2 has mismatched plurals.
Out of your depth is the clear idiom and fits Pocket, but the existing revision lowercases the proper name and is not exact enough for auto-apply.
Neither Calli nor Callie matches the historical prototype name Kali in the filename.
Neither Aces nor Ace names Haze as required by the filename.
Crow and Cow both fail to identify Chrono/Paradox in the missing ping.
Suckers and sucker differ in audible number; a melee kill can be addressed to one victim or the opposing group.
Ah and Oh are distinct audible interjections and cannot be inferred from an upgrade filename.
Was here versus is/Bebop's here changes tense, while is versus apostrophe-s adds contraction ambiguity; filename alone does not resolve it.
I fight and I'll fight are distinct present/future forms; both correctly preserve the authoritative Djinn term.
The astro mapping and authoritative character spelling require Holliday.
Both component revisions are garbled and fail to express a with-Warden teammate ping.
Spirit awaits and spirits await differ in audible number; both are grammatical idol-drop statements.
Although revision 2 spells Yamato correctly, every component revision says is here while the filename requires a was-here ping; none is clearly correct.
